source.title: Epigenetic evolution of deep convolutional models

record.tranche_reason: Uses the cited large-batch generalization concern to motivate its batch-size choice, but does not compare batch sizes or test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The experiments report image-classification fitness for evolved CNNs and offspring before backpropagation. They do not report random-label fitting, training error alongside test error, width sweeps, CNN-versus-fully-connected comparisons, optimizer or batch-size comparisons, dropout comparisons, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. The batch-size discussion cites prior work.
record.test_reason: The study uses the cited large-batch generalization concern to motivate evaluating evolved CNNs at batch size 128, but reports only its framework's performance. It provides no batch-size comparison or other intervention and measurement testing V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that their extended framework can evolve deep CNNs and interpret improving offspring fitness before backpropagation as evidence that crossover transfers learned features. They also introduce variable-shape convolutional kernels and release PyCortex. The speciation advantage remains statistically unconfirmed.
record.recipe_differences: The study evolves CNN structures while training weights with backpropagation; it does not test the original sources' interventions or measurements relevant to these versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Speciation changes offspring fitness before backpropagation; the paper reports higher average overall fitness and average offspring fitness with speciation across the four datasets, while noting that more experiments are needed for statistical significance.

fits_no_version.finding: Table I reports highest test fitness for evolved CNNs with and without speciation across four datasets. These values assess the proposed framework without testing any listed version.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The hybrid neuroevolution framework produces image classifiers with the reported fitness after 100 generations.

fits_no_version.finding: Average population fitness and average offspring fitness before backpropagation are higher with speciation on all four datasets; the authors say further experiments are needed to assess significance. These are separate Table I columns omitted explicitly by the record.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Speciation may improve population performance and preservation of learned features during crossover in this framework.

record.problems: No training-error values are reported, so a train-test gap cannot be assessed. The authors state that more experiments are needed to test the statistical significance of the speciation difference.
record.rows_left_out: The table's average fitness and average offspring fitness before BP columns are not extracted; the rows prioritize highest test fitness, and none of these metrics measures the listed versions. The paper also describes a trend in offspring fitness before BP in the text and Fig. 9, but it does not map to a listed version.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out comparisons.
No controlled width sweep, zero-training-error threshold, or post-interpolation test-error comparison.
No CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison or intervention isolating local connectivity.
Adadelta is used without an SGD comparator or optimizer-tuning comparison.
Batch size is fixed at 128; no comparison establishes a large-batch penalty or its removal under matched epoch budgets.
No dropout or joint dropout-and-weight-decay ablation.
No measured magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization gaps, or ranking against other measures.
No identification and removal of memorized examples followed by retraining against random-removal controls.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains no additional results testing V1–V8. High accuracy at one batch size cannot establish whether larger batches hurt generalization. Because test accuracy is repeatedly used for fitness and selection, the reported test scores are not an untouched final evaluation.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label condition or comparison of training and held-out error.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No fully connected comparator or local-connectivity intervention.
Batch size is 128, but no batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch penalty test.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or other generalization-measure comparison.
No memorized-example identification, removal, or retraining comparison.

rows.stage_stated: trained with standard BP using Adadelta; evolved over 100 generations
rows.operation_detail: Evolution and backpropagation on MNIST; test accuracy used as absolute fitness.
rows.note: The table reports test fitness, not training error or a train-test gap.
rows.check: Numbers match Table I. This is the framework's selected highest fitness at generation 100, not a claim-test result. The test set also drives evolutionary selection. Each generation trains on a random 10% training subset, so 100 generations are not 100 full-data training epochs.
